task.description: Security gate (WF-02 Step 2c equivalent) on ELIXIR-DEV's ISS-0396 implementation, covering the designed fix plus three extensions ELIXIR-DEV flagged as outside the design's own file-touch list: SubProcess.load_parent_context/2's join_counters read, SubProcess.reconcile_parent_projection/5's join_counters write, and persist/8's :event Multi-step reordering.

result.summary:
Read git diff origin/main...HEAD in full (engine.ex, engine/sub_process.ex, engine/task_activation.ex, test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs, docs/anti-patterns.md), the approved design doc, and ISS-0397's actual shipped diff (commits fa041548/86d3d9ea/b5051c15). Ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean) and independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/engine_test.exs test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs test/letflow/engine_complete_task_test.exs test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs` (131 passed, 0 failed) and `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` alone (16 passed) -- both match ELIXIR-DEV's reported counts.

1) DESIGNED FIX (§2): task_activation.ex's append_multi_from_existing_records/6 gains `key_disambiguator \\ nil` exactly as specified; the two unmodified call sites (engine.ex:2674, engine.ex:2009) keep the 6-arg form; sub_process.ex's build_completion_write_steps/12 passes parent_token.id as the sole new-6th-arg call site. Key shapes match the design's own table exactly. Matches design verbatim -- no deviation found.

2) load_parent_context/2 join_counters fix -- claim (a) VERIFIED: read ISS-0397's actual shipped diff (fa041548 design, 86d3d9ea/b5051c15 implementation). It touched only lib/letflow/engine.ex (insert_instance_projection/8, build_instance_state/3, reconcile_projection/5) plus snapshot_writer.ex/instance_projection.ex/migration/tests -- it never touched lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex at all. ELIXIR-DEV's claim that ISS-0397 fixed the engine.ex sibling but missed this sub_process.ex copy is accurate, confirmed by direct diff inspection, not by trusting the anti-patterns.md narrative alone.
   Claim (b) VERIFIED: same mechanism exactly -- `SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters(projection.join_counters)` is the identical public codec function ISS-0397 introduced and engine.ex's build_instance_state/3 already calls; no new codec, no new field.
   Claim (c) VERIFIED: this is a single field read off a struct (`projection`) already fetched earlier in the same function via a plain `Repo.get(InstanceProjection, parent_token.instance_id, prefix: prefix)` -- no recursion, no memoization, no graph traversal. I checked whether ISS-0397 itself underwent reworks for exponential-blowup/memo-key-unsoundness reasons that this read site might inherit: it did not -- ISS-0397's own gate_history (handoffs/WF03-ISS0397-20260901/*.json) shows rework_count: 0 at every step from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR through TEST-RUNNER. The exponential-blowup/memo-key-unsoundness defect class referenced in my task brief actually belongs to ISS-0398/ISS-0400 (walk_to_gateway/find_matching_join graph-traversal fixes, lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md and iss0400-nested-parallel-gateway-fix.md), a structurally unrelated code path (PARALLEL_GATEWAY-join *matching* during graph validation, not join_counters state hydration) that this diff does not touch and load_parent_context/2 never calls into. Flagging this premise correction so it isn't repeated in a future review, but it does not change the verdict: this read site has no recursive or memoized structure to be unsound in the first place.

3) reconcile_parent_projection/5 join_counters write fix -- narrow and same-mechanism: attrs map gains one key, `join_counters: SnapshotWriter.serialize_join_counters(...)`, identical shape/codec to engine.ex's reconcile_projection/5 (ISS-0397 §2.4, 'persisted unconditionally on every call'). Confirmed this function already writes via a plain `Repo.get` + attrs-map update under no lock beyond the transaction's own (same as engine.ex's sibling) -- no new lock/write-time behavior introduced, only an additional field added to an update the transaction was already issuing.

4) persist/8 :event Multi-step reordering -- highest-risk change, given full scrutiny:
   (a) OLD ORDER: :instance_projection (M1) -> :token_record -> children merge -> timer merge -> TaskActivation.append_multi (:task_records) -> :event -> :finalize -> audit merge. The M1 comment's stated reason for :event's old position was never 'the event must reflect post-merge state' -- re-reading the pre-fix comment (git show origin/main:lib/letflow/engine.ex M1 comment) it only asserts 'M4 flips the row to final status right after event append succeeds,' an ordering constraint about :finalize, not about :event needing anything from the children merge.
   (b) EVENT CONTENT: append_instance_started_event/8's callback pattern-matches `fn _repo, _changes ->` -- it reads zero Multi changes, only pre-computed local variables (instance_id, definition, correlation_key, initial_variables, pins, conflicts, attrs, prefix), all bound before Multi.new/0 is even called. Moving its position in the pipe cannot change what it captures -- confirmed by direct read, not inference.
   (c) SCOPE OF EFFECT: this reorders every Engine.create/2 call, not just the 2+-sibling scenario, since it is unconditional pipe-position code. Traced every step between the old and new position for a downstream reader of `changes[:event]`: :token_record, the two Multi.merge steps (children, timers), and TaskActivation.append_multi/6 (which reads only `changes.token_record`) -- none read `changes.event`. :finalize reads only `changes.instance_projection`. Audit merge reads only `changes.finalize`. So no other Multi step's behavior changes for any call shape. The single externally-relevant effect is that EventStore.append/2's active_instance_guard now runs before any code path that can flip instance_projections.status early (SubProcess's own direct write) -- which is the fix's whole point, and is a no-op change for every scenario where nothing flips status before old-:finalize (i.e. every case except the newly-possible synchronous 2+-sibling cascade this design's own test exercises).
   (d) EXISTING TEST COVERAGE: grepped test/ for INSTANCE_STARTED assertions across engine_test.exs, routers/instances_test.exs, engine/pin_rebind_test.exs, engine/timer_wiring_test.exs, engine_sub_process_test.exs -- none assert on Multi-internal step order, only on final DB state (event existence, payload shape, sequence_number via the events table's own auto-increment, event history ordering via the API). Re-ran engine_test.exs (including its 'snapshot written strictly before INSTANCE_STARTED, Multi failure leaves zero other rows' test at line 359, and the REQ-059 pinned_versions/AC4 payload tests) and routers/instances_test.exs and pin_rebind_test.exs directly -- all pass. No silently-wrong-but-passing risk found: sequence_number is assigned by EventStore.append/2's own per-instance counter at INSERT time, unaffected by which Multi step in persist/8 triggers that insert first, since INSTANCE_STARTED is unconditionally this instance's first event regardless of intra-transaction step order.

SECURITY INVARIANTS (INV-1..INV-9), applied per current file guidance (INV-1 live, not default-skip):
- INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES (diff touches Ecto.Multi steps writing instance_projections/tokens/tasks/events rows in engine.ex and engine/sub_process.ex). VERIFIED: (a) every changed/added query is prefix-scoped -- load_parent_context/2's Repo.get(InstanceProjection, ..., prefix: prefix) and its TokenRecord/Task Repo.all(..., prefix: prefix) calls, reconcile_parent_projection/5's Repo.get(..., prefix: prefix) and repo.update (repo already bound to the tenant connection by the caller's transaction), persist/8's :event step's append_instance_started_event(..., prefix) -- all prefix-scoped, none reach the public/default schema; (b) no migration in this diff -- N/A; (c) no tenant_id field written by any changed code in this diff (join_counters/status/variables/current_nodes only) -- N/A. PASS.
- INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; unchanged by this note).
- INV-4 (secrets) -- APPLIES (scope test: general hygiene sweep). `grep -rn \"System.get_env\\|password\\|secret\\|Repo.query\" lib/letflow/engine.ex lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex` -- zero hits. PASS.
- INV-6 (meta) -- satisfied by this handoff's existence with explicit per-invariant reasoning. PASS.
- INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES. `grep -rn \"Repo.query\"` across the three changed files -- zero hits; all changed queries use Ecto.Query/Repo.get/Repo.all with bound prefix, no raw SQL. PASS.
- INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES. `grep -n \"^\\s*{:ok, .*} = \"` across the three changed files -- all hits are pre-existing, unrelated lines inside `case`/`with` clause bodies (pattern-matched branches, not bare top-level destructuring of a fallible external call); none are new code introduced by this diff, and none of the new code (load_parent_context/2's case/with chain, reconcile_parent_projection/5's case, persist/8's Multi.run) introduces a bare-match crash risk -- all failure paths are typed tuples handled by case/with as before. PASS.
- INV-9 (SSRF) -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no outbound HTTP in this diff).

Verdict: no defect found in any of the three extensions or the core fix. All three extensions are genuinely in-family (same struct, same codec, same narrow correctness gap ISS-0397 left, or a pure ordering fix with no content/data change) and correctly scoped. One premise in my own task brief (ISS-0397 '2 reworks' for exponential-blowup/memo-key-unsoundness) does not match ISS-0397's actual history and was corrected above -- it belongs to ISS-0398/ISS-0400 instead, an unrelated code path.
result.routing: Route to Step 3d REVIEWER. PASS -- no BLOCKER found across INV-1/4/6/7/8 (applicable) and INV-2/3/5/9 (not applicable, unaffected). EXPLICIT FLAG FOR REVIEWER, per ELIXIR-DEV's own request: give persist/8's :event Multi-step-reordering its own independent sign-off -- it is the change most likely to have subtle scope-wide effects (it reorders every Engine.create/2 call, not only the 2+-sibling cascade ISS-0396 targets), even though my review found (1) the moved step reads zero `changes` and therefore captures identical event content regardless of position, (2) no other Multi step in persist/8 reads `changes.event`, and (3) the full targeted re-run (131 tests: engine_test.exs, engine_sub_process_test.exs, iss0397_join_counters_test.exs, engine_complete_task_test.exs, routers/instances_test.exs, engine/pin_rebind_test.exs -- all pass) surfaced no regression. REVIEWER should form its own independent judgment on whether this reordering warrants a follow-up issue split rather than riding on ISS-0396's branch, per ELIXIR-DEV's own suggestion in step-03-elixir-dev.json. Also note for REVIEWER: my task brief's premise that ISS-0397 went through 2 reworks for exponential-blowup/memo-key-unsoundness is factually incorrect (ISS-0397's own gate_history shows rework_count: 0 throughout) -- that defect class belongs to ISS-0398/ISS-0400 instead, unrelated to this diff; noted here so it isn't propagated further.

gate_history.notes: All 7 checks pass; independently resolved OQ-2 as moot via transition.ex's find_matching_join/dispatch_parallel_split guard. No rework required.

INV-1/4/6/7/8 applicable and satisfied; INV-2/3/5/9 not applicable. Independently re-ran 131 tests (0 failures) and re-derived the core fix, both join_counters extensions, and the persist/8 reordering against the actual shipped ISS-0397 diff and the real engine.ex code, not just ELIXIR-DEV's narrative. No BLOCKER found.
